high.title: Banks Unanimously Commit to Interest Rate Reduction
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) conducted a meeting where banks unanimously committed to interest rate reductions. SBV's Monetary Policy Department Director Pham Chi Quang reported that in Q1 2026, the central bank operated monetary policy proactively and flexibly to stabilize the macro economy, control inflation, and promote economic growth. SBV conducted flexible open market operations, buying term papers daily with appropriate volumes and diverse maturities to support liquidity and stabilize the money market. Exchange rate and FX market management was aligned with market conditions to absorb shocks, using coordinated monetary policy tools and FX interventions to stabilize the FX market, macro economy and control inflation. For credit management, SBV assigned a 15% credit growth target to support economic recovery while maintaining careful risk control. This coordinated approach signals potential monetary easing ahead if global tensions subside.

high.title: US CPI Surges to Highest in 4 Years in March: Hope for Early Fed Rate Cuts Fading?
high.summary: US CPI jumped 0.9% in March, marking the strongest monthly gain since June 2022 during the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Year-over-year CPI reached 3.3%, up from 2.4% in February. The inflation surge coincided with strong job growth recovery, indicating a stable labor market. However, experts worry prolonged Middle East conflict could damage employment as households tighten spending amid higher prices. The US-Israel-Iran conflict has pushed global oil prices up over 30%, with US retail gasoline exceeding $4/gallon for the first time in over 3 years. This development significantly reduces expectations for early Fed rate cuts and increases pressure on global central banks, including SBV, to maintain hawkish stances. For VND/USD, this supports a stronger dollar and potential pressure on emerging market currencies.

medium.title: Over 16.3 Trillion VND Corporate Bonds Issued in March
medium.summary: March saw significant corporate bond issuance with 11.616 trillion VND in private placements and 4.695 trillion VND in public offerings. March alone accounted for about 2/3 of Q1 total issuance, showing capital flows returning to the bond channel. Notable issuances included EVF's 450 billion VND 8-year bonds at 8.5% fixed rate.

medium.title: Gold Prices Rise Across SJC, PNJ, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau and Bao Tin Manh Hai on April 10
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices increased 1.2-2.2 million VND/tael compared to previous session. Gold bars at major dealers maintained 169.7-172.7 million VND/tael (buy-sell), while gold rings traded at similar levels. The increase reflects global gold price movements amid geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns.

medium.title: ACB Achieves 5.4 Trillion VND Profit in Q1, Chairman Tran Hung Huy Addresses Au Lac Shareholder Group
medium.summary: ACB reported Q1 2026 pre-tax profit of 5.4 trillion VND, up 56% QoQ and 17% YoY. Credit grew 3.2% and deposits increased 1%. The bank completed 24% of annual profit target. Management noted limited impact from Middle East geopolitical tensions on banking operations.

medium.title: SGI Capital: Capital Flows Increasingly Sensitive to Interest Rates, Prioritizing Defense Awaiting Opportunities
medium.summary: SGI Capital assesses prolonged supply chain disruption risks are becoming more likely, negatively impacting global economy. Rising oil prices above $90 create negative effects on inflation and growth prospects. Bond markets signal rising interest rates under inflationary pressure, making capital flows increasingly defensive and sensitive to rates.
